# Hydration notes

Quick reference for how dough handling changes as water percentage goes up, since I keep having to
relearn this every few months.

- 65-70%: easy to shape, tighter crumb, forgiving for a first attempt
- 75%: the sweet spot for a normal weeknight loaf, still handleable on a lightly floured board
- 80-85%: open, irregular crumb if it works, but the dough is slack and wants wet hands, not flour,
  during shaping
- 90%+: closer to batter than dough; only tried this once, see [[sourdough-hydration]] for the
  longer writeup

Higher hydration also ferments faster, since there's more water available for enzyme activity, so
the bulk rise needs watching rather than trusting the clock.
